title: Goa opinion pol/ referendum done and majority 55.48% supported the decision not to merge with Maharashtra.
text: The Goa Opinion Poll Day, also known as Asmitai Dis, was a referendum held in newly annexed union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu in India, on 16 January 1967, to deal with the Konkani language agitation and to decide the future of Goa. The referendum, backed by United Goans Party, offered the people of Goa a choice between continuing as a separate territory of India, or merging with the large Marathi speaking sta…

title: 17–21 February - 1967 Indian general election, Indian National Congress came back into power despite facing set back in various states.
text: General elections were held in India between 17 and 21 February 1967 to elect 520 of the 523 members of the fourth Lok Sabha, an increase of 15 from the previous session of Lok Sabha. Elections to State Assemblies were also held simultaneously, the last general election to do so.

title: India and Myanmar enters into a border agreement which demarcates India–Myanmar border.
text: The India–Myanmar border is the international border between India and Myanmar. The 1,643 kilometres (1,021 mi) long border runs from the tripoint with China in the north to the tripoint with Bangladesh in the south.

title: Congress Working Committee adopted a resolution for social control of banks, nationalization of general insurance, removal of princes privileges.
text: The Congress Working Committee is the executive committee of the Indian National Congress. It was formed in December 1920 at Nagpur session of INC which was headed by C. Vijayaraghavachariar.

title: Zakir Husain becomes the first Muslim to become president of India.
text: Zakir Husain Khan was an Indian educationist and politician who served as the vice president of India from 1962 to 1967 and president of India from 13 May 1967 until his death on 3 May 1969. text: West Bengal is a state in the eastern part of India. It is situated along the Bay of Bengal.

title: Indira Gandhi announces Ten Point Program a Socialistic roadmap during All India Congress Committee meet.
text: Indira Priyadarshini Gandhi was an Indian stateswoman who twice served as the Prime Minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984. She was India's first and only female prime minister, and a central figure in Indian politics as the leader of the Indian National Congress (INC).

title: Indian and Chinese troops begin to exchange fire at Nathu La in Sikkim. This event is known as the Nathu La and Cho La clashes
text: Sikkim is a state in northeast India. It borders Bhutan in the east, the Tibet Autonomous Region of China in the north and northeast, Koshi Province of Nepal in the west, and West Bengal in the south.

title: Indian and Chinese troops clash in Cho La and the duel ended after a day.
text: Cho La or Cho-la is a mountain pass in the Chola range of the Himalayas. It connects the Indian state of Sikkim with China's Tibet Autonomous Region.

title: Kerala State Lotteries becomes the first state to start Lottery under public sector.
text: Kerala State Lotteries is a lottery programme run by the Government of Kerala. Established in 1967, under the lottery department of the Government of Kerala, it is the first of its kind in India.

title: The 6.6 .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Mw Koynanagar earthquake shook western India with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing 177–180 and injuring 2,272.
text: The Modified Mercalli intensity scale measures the effects of an earthquake at a given location. This is in contrast with the seismic magnitude usually reported for an earthquake.
